title: Integral open and closed pieces remain constructible and rationalize to the localization sequence
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]; noetherian means a finite affine cover by spectra of noetherian rings, and finite-dimensional means a finite bound on lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets. Write $A_Y(V)=C(|V|,A)$ and $E_Y(V)=C(|V|,E)$ on the small pro-etale site of any locally closed subscheme $Y$ of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use sheaf modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $S_Y(M)=E_Y\otimes_{A_Y}M$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Constructible integral means continuous-constructible as in [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module], with local models $A_Y\otimes_A P$ for finitely presented $A$-modules $P$ on finitely many locally closed strata. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Use the module inverse images, direct image and extension by zero of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], with coefficient rings on the subschemes identified by [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. If $M_U$ and $M_Z$ are constructible integral sheaves on $U$ and $Z$, then $Q=j_!M_U$ and $P=i_*M_Z$ are constructible integral sheaves on $X$, and
$$S_XQ\cong j_!S_UM_U,\qquad S_XP\cong i_*S_ZM_Z.$$
If $L$ is any $E_X$-module sheaf with specified isomorphisms $S_UM_U\cong j^{-1}L$ and $S_ZM_Z\cong i^{-1}L$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], these comparisons identify the canonical open-closed sequence with a short exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow S_XQ\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow S_XP\longrightarrow0$$
[def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

source.place: Lemma 6.8.13, constructible filtration and extension assembly; Stacks Tags 09AH (proetale.tex, lemma-ses-associated-to-open), 09AA (lemma-closed-immersion), 09BN (lemma-open-immersion) and 03DI (sites-modules.tex, lemma-extension-by-zero).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], $|X|$ has the descending-chain condition on closed subsets: a strictly descending chain would contradict a minimal element of the set of its terms. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets], every subset of $|X|$ is quasi-compact. In particular $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact for every affine open $V\subset X$, which is exactly quasi-compactness of $j$. Thus the complementary-immersion hypotheses of the ringed open/closed lemma hold, including for $U=\varnothing$ or $Z=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 09AH (lemma-ses-associated-to-open), quasi-compactness hypothesis; properties.tex Tag 01OZ (lemma-Noetherian-topology) and topology.tex Tag 04ZA (lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact).

proof.text: Choose a finite locally closed stratification $(U_a)$ adapted to $M_U$ by [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Regard each $U_a\hookrightarrow U\hookrightarrow X$ as the same locally closed stratum in $X$ and append $Z$; these are disjoint and cover $X$, so form a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification]. For $Q=j_!M_U$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] gives $j^{-1}Q\cong M_U$ and $i^{-1}Q=0$. On an old stratum the restriction of $Q$ is therefore the given restriction of $M_U$: inverse-image composition and its module structures are compatible by [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison]. The coefficient isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] identify these inverse images with ringed restrictions over $A_{U_a}$. Retain exactly the old pro-etale covering family and its finitely presented $A$-modules. On $Z$, the restricted module is zero, with local model $A_Z\otimes_A0=0$; the zero $A$-module is finitely presented. This proves continuous integral constructibility of $Q$ directly from the definition.

source.place: Tags 09AA, 09AH, 09AG: restrictions of extension by zero; agent expansion using Bhatt-Scholze Definition 6.8.10

proof.text: Choose an adapted finite stratification $(Z_b)$ for $M_Z$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Its strata, embedded in $X$ by composition with $i$, together with $U$, are disjoint locally closed subsets covering $X$ [def-constructible-stratification]. For $P=i_*M_Z$, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] gives $i^{-1}P\cong M_Z$ and $j^{-1}P=0$. Thus each $Z_b$ has exactly the old local models, by inverse-image composition [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] and the continuous coefficient identifications [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. The added open stratum $U$ has model $A_U\otimes_A0=0$. These finitely many strata and their given covering families witness constructibility of $P$. Empty strata may be discarded, so neither empty complementary locus causes an exception.

source.place: Tags 09AA and 09AH: closed direct image and disjoint open restriction; agent expansion using Bhatt-Scholze Definition 6.8.10

proof.text: Identify the open site with the slice at $U$ by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Apply the ordinary formula [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] with ring $A_X$, open module $M_U$ and ambient module $E_X$. Commuting the two tensor factors gives an $A_X$-linear isomorphism $T:=E_X\otimes_{A_X}j_!M_U\cong j_!((j^{-1}E_X)\otimes_{j^{-1}A_X}M_U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction], the module inside is $S_UM_U$. To specify the canonical map as well, use the tensor restriction comparison [lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] to identify $j^{-1}T$ with $S_UM_U$. The open counit $j_!j^{-1}T\to T$ is an isomorphism: the preceding formula places $T$ in the essential image of $j_!$, and $j^{-1}j_!\cong\mathrm{id}$ from [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] makes this counit invertible by the adjunction triangle identities. Its inverse is the desired comparison $S_XQ\cong j_!S_UM_U$, normalized to the identity on restriction to $U$. This is also $E_X$-linear. Indeed both extensions by zero have the same underlying sheafification construction, and on local pure tensors the counit sends $e\otimes m$ to $e\otimes m$, so multiplication by a local section $b$ of $E_X$ on either side sends it to $(be)\otimes m$. The equality respects restrictions and passes to sheafification.

source.place: Tag 0E8I (sites-modules.tex, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); open adjunction and coefficient restriction. The normalization is an agent argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-closed-underived-projection] with $R=A_X$, $B=E_X$, $F=E_X$ and $M=M_Z$. After tensor symmetry it gives the canonical $E_X$-linear isomorphism $E_X\otimes_{A_X}i_*M_Z\cong i_*((i^{-1}E_X)\otimes_{i^{-1}A_X}M_Z)$. Compose with the coefficient isomorphisms $i^{-1}A_X\cong A_Z$ and $i^{-1}E_X\cong E_Z$ of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction], compatible with $A\to E$. The result is $S_XP\cong i_*S_ZM_Z$. The chosen projection map restricts, under the closed counit, to the identity on $E_Z\otimes_{A_Z}M_Z$, as follows from its explicit adjunct in the new lemma. No derived tensor, flatness or degree-zero identification is used.

source.place: Tags 09AA and 09AH, and sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL; agent-formulated underived closed projection consequence

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] to the ring $E_X$ and module $L$ to obtain $0\to j_!j^{-1}L\xrightarrow{\epsilon_L}L\xrightarrow{\eta_L}i_*i^{-1}L\to0$. Write $\alpha:S_UM_U\cong j^{-1}L$ and $\beta:S_ZM_Z\cong i^{-1}L$ for the specified isomorphisms, and $c_U:S_XQ\cong j_!S_UM_U$, $c_Z:S_XP\cong i_*S_ZM_Z$ for Steps 4 and 5. Define the first arrow to be $\epsilon_L\circ j_!(\alpha)\circ c_U$ and the second arrow to be $c_Z^{-1}\circ i_*(\beta^{-1})\circ\eta_L$. These formulas give an isomorphism of this three-term sequence with the canonical open/closed sequence, including both end maps. Hence it is short exact, and the comparisons identify it with that canonical sequence as asserted. This retains the correct sequence also for the zero sheaf and either empty complementary locus.

The item statement is unchanged and the clause-restating helper is gone. Step 1: the noetherian minimal-element and compact-subsets lemmas give quasi-compactness of j (Stacks 01OZ/04ZA), the hypothesis the ringed open/closed lemma needs. Steps 2 and 3: constructibility is proved straight from Definition 6.8.10 by keeping the old strata (locally closed in X because U is open and Z is closed), adding the complementary stratum with the zero model, and using j^-1 j_! = id, i^-1 j_! = 0, i^-1 i_* = id, j^-1 i_* = 0, gamma composition and the coefficient identifications. Step 4: the existing lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor (Stacks 0E8I) is reused; the two j_! constructions agree by localization (4). The canonical map is the inverse of the counit, which is invertible by the triangle identity, and the E_X-linearity check is accepted. Step 5: the new node lem-weil-pbc-proetale-closed-underived-projection is applied with R=A_X and F=B=E_X. It is true: j^-1 of the source is 0, so the localization unit is an iso, and i^-1 of the source is M tensor i^-1 F by sigma and the counit. It is a generic underived tool, not a clause of the item. The only near matches are derived nodes (lem-weil-proetale-closed-tensor-projection, lem-sfb-ringed-projection-tensor-composition, lem-sf-etale-generic-immersion-projection). All three Mathlib search kinds are recorded. Step 6: explicit arrows epsilon_L∘j_!(alpha)∘c_U and c_Z^-1∘i_*(beta^-1)∘eta_L, directions correct. No derived tensor or scalar-model bridge is used (C5). Accepted tool_use: lem-pur-proetale-inverse-image-tensor-comparison, for sigma/gamma coherence only.
